nodes.name: FeCoNi alloy melting
nodes.procedure: The FeCoNi alloy was obtained by melting in an induction furnace from high-purity metal particles of iron (99.90%), cobalt (99.95%), and nickel (99.99%) as raw materials according to different weight ratios (Fe:Co:Ni = 2:4:4 / 4:3:3 / 6:2:2 / 8:1:1). Here, the ratio of Co/Ni was kept unchanged at 1:1, but the proportions of Fe/Co and Fe/Ni varied from 2:4 to 8:1.
nodes.source_text: Sample preparation: The FeCoNi alloy was obtained by melting in an induction furnace from high-purity metal particles...

nodes.name: Fe0.4Co0.3Ni0.3 alloy hydrothermal oxidation (1.8M)
nodes.procedure: The obtained alloy plate surfaces were ground with 200, 320, and 500 grit sandpapers, ultrasonically cleaned in absolute ethanol, and then put into 1 M hydrochloric acid for 5 min pickling and activation. Afterward, they were taken out, washed with deionized water, and placed in a Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave filled with alkaline oxidation solutions consisting of 3.6 M sodium hydroxide and 1.8 M hydrogen peroxide (molar ratio 2:1). The container was sealed and put in the electric thermostatic box. The box temperature was raised to 180°C and kept at this temperature for 18 h to conduct hydrothermal reaction. After completion, the container was cooled naturally to room temperature. The plates were taken out, rinsed by deionized water and absolute ethanol, and then dried with cold air to obtain the catalytic electrode.

nodes.description: Overall water splitting stability with FeCoNi-1.8 anode and Pt cathode
nodes.source_text: When the as-prepared Fe₀.₄Co₀.₃Ni₀.₃-1.8 electrode is used as the anode and the platinum electrode as the cathode... exhibits excellent stability with a negligible OER η₁₀ increase of 3.3 mV after 48 h testing... η₅₀ increases only 17 mV

To assess the ECSA... of the oxidized Fe₀.₄Co₀.₃Ni₀.₃ catalytic electrode, the double-layer capacitance C_dl was measured by the cyclic voltammogram (CV) curves recorded at scan rate from 10 to 120 mV S⁻¹... The Fe₀.₄Co₀.₃Ni₀.₃-1.8 sample consistently exhibits the maximum ECSA

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows mixed nanosheet and nanorod morphology with dimensions <100 nm contributing to large ECSA for the Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 catalytic electrode.
nodes.evidence_snippet: H_2O_2 concentration reaching 1.8M, the surface micro structure changes to a mixed pattern containing nanosheets and nanorods. Both the diameter of the nanorods and the thickness of the nanosheets are less than 100nm, which helps to obtain a larger specific surface area.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX line scanning shows Ni enrichment in top ~2 μm surface layer of Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 with surface composition Ni 66.88 at.%, Fe 15.22 at.%, Co 3.34 at.% and uniform transverse elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectra were collected from three random regions on the sample surface... and the element percentage data show much higher Ni (Avg. 66.88 at.%) content than Fe (Avg. 15.22 at.%) and Co (Avg. 3.34 at.%)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 shows largest number of diffraction peaks corresponding to multivalent oxides and hydroxides of Fe, Co, Ni indicating most abundant catalytic species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 exhibits diffraction peaks of the largest number, indicating that the corresponding catalytic species on the surface are the most abundant

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals surface Ni enrichment (Ni>Fe>Co) with atomic percentages Ni>Fe>Co, mixed bivalent/trivalent states of Fe/Co/Ni, and O 1s showing OH^- at surface transitioning to O^{2-} at 40 nm depth for Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8.
nodes.evidence_snippet: for the oxidized Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3} samples, the surface content of the elements followed the same order: Ni > Fe > Co under any H_2O_2... O mainly exists in the form of OH^- at the outermost layer, and O^{2-} while reaching the depth of 40 nm O^{2-}.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faradaic region (0.05-0.20 V vs RHE) at 10-120 mV s^{-1} shows Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 has maximum double-layer capacitance C_{dl} and thus maximum ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the double-layer capacitance C_dl was measured by the cyclic voltammogram (CV) curves recorded at scan rate from 10 to 120mV S^{-1} in the non-Faradaic region within a potential window of 0.05 - 0.20V vs. RHE. The Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 sample consistently exhibits the maximum ECSA

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 has lowest charge transfer resistance R_ct of 1.30 Ω cm² for OER and 1.04 Ω cm² for HER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is validated that the Fe_{0.4}Co_{0.3}Ni_{0.3}-1.8 sample possesses the lowest charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of 1.30Ω cm² in OER process and 1.04Ω cm² in HER process among all the samples
